name: Community phishing investigation and reporting tools
scope: Tools the maintainers use, credited independently from configured data feeds. Non-exhaustive; not a ranking or partnership list.
access_notes: Many basic web functions are free without registration. Account requirements, quotas and paid features differ by provider. See each service and its references.
visibility_notes: Public scans may expose submitted URLs. A clean verdict is not a guarantee; reporting does not guarantee blocking or removal.

tools.name: Bitdefender Link Checker
tools.description: Check an individual link against phishing, fraudulent-site and malware signals.
tools.note: The browser checker is free; other Bitdefender products are separate.

tools.name: crt.sh
tools.description: Search public certificate-transparency records for domain names and related certificates.
tools.note: A certificate is an infrastructure clue, not a trust or safety verdict.

tools.name: DNSDumpster
tools.description: Explore DNS records and related hosts to understand a domain’s exposed infrastructure.
tools.note: Free membership and paid plans have different quotas. Follow current access requirements.

tools.name: Google Safe Browsing
tools.description: Send a suspected phishing page to Google for review by its Safe Browsing service.
tools.note: Submit the suspicious URL and relevant context. Google decides its own classification.

tools.name: isitphish
tools.description: Get an automated phishing assessment to support your investigation of a suspicious URL.
tools.note: A free plan is advertised. Check current account and usage requirements.

tools.name: Microsoft Security Intelligence
tools.description: Report a phishing page or other unsafe website through Microsoft’s guest submission form.
tools.note: No account needed for this guest route; the form includes a verification challenge.

tools.name: Netcraft
tools.description: Send suspected phishing, malware and suspicious URLs to Netcraft’s reporting service.
tools.note: Use the report form’s requested details; Netcraft reviews submissions under its own process.

tools.name: Norton Safe Web
tools.description: Consult Norton’s website reputation information as another signal in a URL investigation.
tools.note: Lookup and account-based participation are different functions; follow the service’s current access rules.

tools.name: phish.report
tools.description: Analyse suspected phishing, inspect hosting context and find reporting routes.
tools.note: Free tools for individual volunteers, nonprofits and governments; team plans are separate.

tools.name: Phishs
tools.description: Check URLs for phishing and malicious content, and inspect the resulting risk report.
tools.note: Public scanner; API and expanded features have separate plans.

tools.name: PhishTank
tools.description: Browse community phishing reports, contribute a suspected phish and help verify reports.
tools.note: Browsing is public. Submitting and verifying require sign-in.

tools.name: PolySwarm
tools.description: Explore URL and file intelligence from multiple threat-detection engines.
tools.note: A free Community account unlocks more functions. Quotas and paid tiers apply.

tools.name: Quttera
tools.description: Scan publicly accessible website content for suspicious scripts and malicious code.
tools.note: Provide a URL to start. Remote scanning has coverage and processing limits.

tools.name: ScamAdviser
tools.description: Review website trust signals and community context when assessing a suspicious site.
tools.note: Treat reputation scores as context; a favorable score is not proof of safety.

tools.name: Spamhaus
tools.description: Investigate IP and domain reputation through Spamhaus’s public resources and checker.
tools.note: Public lookups and commercial data use have separate conditions.

tools.name: Sucuri SiteCheck
tools.description: Check visible website content for malware, blocklist status and common security issues.
tools.note: The public checker does not inspect hidden server-side files.

tools.name: Symantec Site Review
tools.description: Look up a URL’s category and request a review when its classification appears incorrect.
tools.note: Category review is a provider assessment, not a website takedown.

tools.name: urlquery
tools.description: Inspect website activity, potential malware and reputation through URL analysis reports.
tools.note: Report visibility and account features vary; check the selected submission settings.

tools.name: urlscan.io
tools.description: Capture browser behavior, contacted infrastructure and page evidence, or search existing scans.
tools.note: Anonymous use has limits. Accounts add features; public scans are visible to others.

tools.name: VirusTotal
tools.description: Compare URL assessments and inspect domain context across multiple security sources.
tools.note: Web queries may enter the shared dataset. API access requires an account; usage terms apply.

tools.name: Yandex Search
tools.description: Use Yandex Search’s feedback route to report spam or malicious pages in search.
tools.note: Use the embedded form and its current requirements; this is not a universal takedown service.
